topics.label: Introduction and Course Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series, introduces the lecturer, and outlines the key learning outcomes regarding environmental exposures and cancer development.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer: Intrinsic Factors, Environment, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the fundamental nature of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease while weighing intrinsic cellular errors against environmental exposures through epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how microbial and viral infections drive oncogenesis, illustrated in depth by the epidemiology and molecular mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the biochemical and molecular pathways through which physical radiation and chemical carcinogens induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental life stages influence cancer progression.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey the analytical, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methods used to identify carcinogen exposure and evaluate mutagenic potential.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by summarising the balance of everyday risks versus benefits regarding environmental carcinogen exposure.
